[RDSC.9.12] **A string field holds well-formed UTF-8 and no U+0000.** A
loader **must** refuse with `DS_ERR_DSC_DECODE` an atom body in which a field
of protobuf type `string`, at any depth it reads ([RDSC.11.4]), holds bytes
that are not well-formed UTF-8 (RFC 3629), or that hold U+0000, which no
`String` holds ([LSTR.1.1]). Protobuf's own decode of a proto3 `string` field
refuses ill-formed UTF-8 at the occurrence that holds it, so such a body has
not decoded, and it is refused before any other rule judges it. A
field that occurs more than once is judged at every occurrence. A loader
**must not** repair the string, nor truncate it at a U+0000.

**Two `bytes` fields carry text, and are judged as strings.** Where a
loader reads them, it **must** refuse the same way an atom body whose
`proto/ds_source.proto#DsSource` `data`, the module's source text
([RDSC.14.2.1]), or whose `proto/schema_def.proto#SchemaDef` `proto_source`,
the schema's `.proto` text ([RDSC.5.8.3]), is not well-formed UTF-8 or holds
U+0000. This clause reaches no other `bytes` field. A loader reads either
field as text only when its body's `compression` is `COMPRESSION_NONE`. Under
any other, it refuses the body for its compression ([RDSC.4.5.1]) and reads
no text. What it judges is the field's value, which for a field that occurs
more than once is its last occurrence ([RDSC.9.5]).

No conforming compiler writes such a string: every name it emits is an
identifier ([LNAM.2]), every literal a `String` ([LSTR.1.1]), and the source
and `.proto` texts are UTF-8 ([LLEX.1.1]). This is a
cheap structural need of the loader's ([RDSC.9.9]), one pass over each string
it reads.
